architecture.mechanism: Gravity-driven multi-barrier filtration exploiting natural sedimentation, bio-sand filtration, and plant-based coagulation (e.g., Moringa oleifera seed powder) to simultaneously aggregate suspended sediments and inactivate pathogens via adsorption and natural antimicrobial compounds.
architecture.intervention: A three-zone vessel: (1) upper settling chamber with dose-controlled Moringa seed powder dispenser for coagulation/flocculation of sediments; (2) middle bio-sand layer (fine sand, charcoal, gravel) for physical filtration and biofilm development; (3) lower ceramic candle filter (locally fired clay with sawdust burnout pores) for final polishing. All materials locally sourced; no replaceable cartridges.
architecture.expected_effect: >95% turbidity reduction (target <5 NTU) and >99.9% E. coli reduction (target <1 CFU/100 mL) at 10–20 L/day household flow rate, sustained for 6 months without media replacement.
architecture.falsification_test: Challenge with synthetic high-turbidity water (200 NTU kaolin + 10^6 CFU/mL E. coli) at 2× design flow for 14 consecutive days; fail if output turbidity >10 NTU or E. coli >10 CFU/100 mL on any day.
